question: Which of the following is an ABSOLUTE indication for securing a definitive (cuffed endotracheal) airway?

answers.text: SpO2 90% on a 28% Venturi mask in a stable COPD patient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An SpO2 of 90% on controlled low-flow oxygen in a stable COPD patient may be the acceptable target range and does not itself mandate intubation.

answers.text: Respiratory rate of 24 breaths/min with mild anxiety in a post-operative patient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tachypnoea with mild anxiety may warrant close monitoring and non-invasive support but is not an absolute indication for intubation.

answers.text: Loss of airway protective reflexes with inability to maintain own airway

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Loss of protective reflexes (e.g., in Glasgow Coma Scale ≤8 or complete loss of gag/cough) with inability to maintain airway patency is an absolute indication for definitive airway securement.

answers.text: Expected surgical procedure lasting more than 2 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Surgical duration alone is not an absolute indication. Many procedures >2 hours are safely performed with supraglottic airways (LMA) or regional anaesthesia without intubation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the absolute indications for advanced airway management. Loss of protective reflexes, inability to oxygenate with basic manoeuvres, and predicted airway deterioration are the key categories.
Correct. Loss of protective airway reflexes is one of the key absolute indications for a definitive airway — the cuffed ETT is the gold standard in this scenario.
